feature: gRFC A6 concurrent unary hedging on SharedChannel

explicit_boundaries: ordinary single-owner Channel rejects concurrent hedging
client-streaming, server-streaming, and bidirectional calls reject hedging without a complete replay buffer

reference.specification: gRFC A6 client retries and hedging
reference.observed_boundary: the pinned grpc-core C++ retry filter and parser still contain explicit TODOs for implementing hedging; Netz follows normative gRFC A6 semantics and exceeds that local C++ implementation boundary
normative_contract: the original attempt starts immediately and later attempts start after hedgingDelay up to maxAttempts
a non-fatal response accelerates the next hedge, a fatal or OK response wins, and all losers are canceled
positive pushback replaces the next delay while malformed or negative pushback stops new hedges
retry throttling always permits the first attempt and gates later hedges at the half-token threshold
all attempts share one RPC deadline and the last non-fatal response is returned after exhaustion
retryPolicy and hedgingPolicy are mutually exclusive

implementation.parser: owned service config requires maxAttempts >= 2, clamps to 5, accepts absent or zero hedgingDelay, validates unique non-OK nonFatalStatusCodes, and rejects retry/hedging ambiguity
implementation.scheduler: one bounded std.Io.Select owns at most five attempt tasks plus generation-stamped timers; stale timers are ignored after acceleration or pushback
implementation.attempts: every physical job advertises remaining grpc-timeout and grpc-previous-rpc-attempts, retains one transparent REFUSED_STREAM recovery, and resolves request hash independently at the physical-attempt boundary
implementation.winner: OK or fatal completion cancels and joins all outstanding jobs before response ownership returns; loser cancellation reuses SharedChannel stream-scoped RST_STREAM cleanup
implementation.non_fatal: non-fatal status or configured backend-local UNAVAILABLE-class transport failure accelerates the next attempt; final exhaustion returns the last response or last transport error
implementation.pushback: retry and hedging share a strict signed-int32 canonical grpc-retry-pushback-ms parser with no plus sign or redundant leading zeros
implementation.throttling: first attempt always runs; later timers and acceleration require a balance above half; qualifying failures debit one token and an OK winner replenishes tokenRatio
implementation.deadline: running attempts and pending pushback timers share one awake-clock absolute deadline and cannot renew it
implementation.streaming_boundary: ordinary Channel and all streaming APIs reject hedging explicitly instead of silently serializing or ignoring the policy

native_cases: valid/default/clamped hedgingPolicy parsing and owned status arrays
missing or too-small maxAttempts, malformed delay, OK/duplicate/unknown non-fatal statuses, and retryPolicy conflict
50 ms delayed second attempt wins on another endpoint and the first endpoint observes exact RST_STREAM CANCEL
UNAVAILABLE without pushback bypasses a two-second delay immediately
positive 150 ms pushback replaces the two-second delay
negative pushback prevents a second endpoint from receiving a request
pre-exhausted retry throttle prevents a scheduled second hedge
two non-fatal attempts return the deliberately delayed final response
backend-local connection errors are separated from OOM and validation failures
service-config activation, direct API activation, ordinary Channel rejection, and Shared streaming rejection

results.grpc_cpp_release_fast: 9/9 build steps passed over h2c and certificate-verified TLS
results.reference_status: grpc-core C++ has no complete hedging runner at the pinned revision, so gRFC A6 is normative and real Netz multi-endpoint tests provide the behavioral proof

remaining_gap: hedging is complete for replay-safe unary calls on the concurrent SharedChannel owner; adding it to ordinary Channel would require changing that type's single-owner contract, and arbitrary streaming RPCs still require an application-defined replay buffer
